title: Interface primitives stacking and naming taxonomy refresh
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Reduce friction for engineers and designers by standardizing stacking behavior, spacing heuristics, and name taxonomy across the UI kit so tokens and primitives compose reliably in product screens.

Scope:
- Audit a representative slice of primitives (buttons, input atoms, table row atoms, chart legends) for stack behavior and cross-breakpoint resizing.
- Normalize auto-layout direction and gap attributes so a small set of patterns cover >90% of use cases.
- Introduce a concise naming taxonomy for primitives and their states (semantic -> visual mapping) and move obsolete instances to an archived page.
- Publish a checklist and a gated library release (soft-deprecate old variants with clear migration notes).

Out-of-scope: full token migration (separate ticket), screens-level redesign.

Deliverables:
- Figma file updates (Interface Primitives v2 page) and a migration guide (.md) for developers.
- Release checklist with QA steps, plus a small set of snippet examples for common layout patterns.
- Follow-up list of cleanup tickets for any remaining edge-case variants.

Acceptance criteria:
- All primitives use one of three documented auto-layout patterns with explicit gap tokens.
- Naming follows the new taxonomy and is searchable (preview in figma search).
- Library publish does not break 80% of existing production usages (verified via quick grep of component names in repo and 3 sample product pages).
- Migration guide linked in release notes and shared with platform team.
